newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end narrowly lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end narrowly lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks remained locked in a tight band Thursday and closed with a small insignificant loss, dealers said.
"The market is very calmly performing a downward correction and obviously does not fear the U.S. jobs report due out tomorrow," dealers said.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.2 percent to 788.86, recording its fourth loss in nearly four weeks.
Turnover slowed to 24 million pesos from 31.4 million Wednesday and a strong average tally of 40 million in the previous three sessions.
Over-the-counter turnover dwindled to 76.6 million pesos from 112.3 million Wednesday.
"When the MerVal reached 800 points (Tuesday) it triggered sell programs, but the market is absorbing this round of profit-taking well," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli.

"Although foreign investors may not have fully digested this news yet, economic growth in Argentina is strongly outpacing forecasts and pushing up the year-end MerVal target closer to 1,000 points than the original 800-850."
Traders said the bolsa remained underpinned by corporate news including major purchases and mergers announced in May.
The broad market index closed off 0.1 percent in the session, with winners edging out losers 28 to 27 and 27 stocks ending flat.
Main-tier gains were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Polledo and carmaker Ciadea, which rallied 6.7 percent, 3.5 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which shed 2.2 percent, and foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata, real estate developer Irsa and carmaker Sevel, all off 1.5 percent.
